newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing Enterprises steals show on Hong Kong debut.
newsitem.headline: Beijing Enterprises steals show on Hong Kong debut.

text.p: China's latest red chip stock burst into action on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on Thursday, more than trebling in price on its first day of trade while the rest of the market was left in the dust.

Days of anticipation over Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd's stock market debut unleashed a mad scramble for its shares, which skyrocketed to a high of HK$45.00 (US$5.81) soon after the opening bell on Thursday before closing at HK$40.20.
The stock was issued at HK$12.48.
"It reflects people's confidence in Hong Kong after the handover," Beijing Enterprises chairman Hu Zhao Guang told traders at the company's listing ceremony on Thursday.

The red chip conglomerate, controlled by Beijing's municipal government, launched a 150 million share global initial public offering last week amid a stampede for China-linked stocks ahead of Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on July 1.
Thousands of retail investors queued for hours last week to get their applications in, driving the subscription level for the Hong Kong offering to a record high for the territory.
The 13.5 million shares offered to the Hong Kong public were a massive 1,276 times subscribed, tying up about HK$215 billion in Hong Kong's banking system.
Beijing Enteprises also offered 135 million shares to international investors and 1.5 million to its employees.
The overwhelming response to its share issue prompted the company to boost its retail offering, with 51.75 million shares finally allocated to the Hong Kong public and employees.
The huge appetite for Beijing Enterprises shares stems from its connections to the Chinese capital, analysts said.
Beijing Enteprises is 69 percent owned by Beijing Holdings Ltd, the primary trading and commercial vehicle in Hong Kong of the Beijing municipal government. Hu is vice-mayor of Beijing.
"There is optimism towards the handover, Chinese growth is rising and people know there is going to be asset injections there," said Robert Rountree, regional strategist at Nomura Research Institute.

While Beijing Enterprises dominated trade on Thursday, contributing HK$2.5 billion to total market turnover of HK$16.39 billion, the blue-chip Hang Seng index tumbled 139.91 points, or 0.96 percent, to 14,416.57.
"Nobody cares about blue chips today. Most of the blue chips are down," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at BNP PrimeEast Securities.
He said gains in Beijing Enterprises shares had been capped by some investors locking in huge profits.
"They made around HK$26 on each share," said Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities.
Analysts said some investors were also hesitating before jumping in at such a high price.

"A lot of people probably can't bring themselves to pay HK$40 for the stock but they will want it in their portfolio eventually. It's just too good of a chance to miss," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
